messages.content: The flights are settled for now, so I need the hotel portion for Raleigh. I need four nights, Monday April 15 through Friday April 19, near the audit site in Morrisville.

What is the audit-site address or nearest intersection, and what nightly rate cap should I use? I will also check Monday late-arrival handling and whether the hotel issues an itemized receipt suitable for a business expense report.
The site is at 1000 Perimeter Park Drive in Morrisville. The cap is $210 per night before taxes. I have to be onsite by 8:00 a.m. Tuesday through Friday.

I found three practical options within the cap for April 15-19. Hyatt House Raleigh Durham Airport is about 8-12 minutes from the site and is showing approximately $184 nightly. Holiday Inn Express Raleigh-Durham Airport is roughly 10-15 minutes away at about $169. Four Points by Sheraton Raleigh Durham Airport is around 12-18 minutes away at about $191. Those commute estimates are for ordinary morning traffic, so I would allow 25 minutes on the first audit day.
Compare the Hyatt House and the Holiday Inn Express. I do not need a suite comparison. I mainly want to know whether either creates an issue if the flight is delayed Monday night.

Both advertise a staffed front desk and accept late arrivals, but the reservation should be marked for late check-in so the room is not treated as a no-show. Hyatt House lists check-in from 3:00 p.m.; Holiday Inn Express also lists a 3:00 p.m. start. Neither publishes a specific arrival cutoff, so for a delay past midnight I would call the property directly after booking and have the confirmation annotated.
What about the business receipt? I need room rate, taxes, and incidentals separated. A credit-card total by itself will not pass review.

Both properties can provide a hotel folio at checkout showing nightly room charges, taxes, and separately posted incidentals. That is the itemized document you would submit rather than the card receipt. Direct booking makes the process straightforward; a prepaid third-party rate can complicate the lodging-charge portion of the folio.
Then use direct rates only. Are parking or breakfast charges likely to push either one over the cap?

The displayed direct rates for both remain below the $210 pre-tax room cap. Both currently list self-parking and breakfast without a separate daily charge, though those inclusions should be confirmed in the final rate details because packages can differ. Hyatt House would leave about $26 of room-rate headroom; Holiday Inn Express would leave about $41.
The commute matters more than the extra $15. Is the Hyatt House clearly better for an 8:00 start, or are they effectively the same?

They are close, but Hyatt House has the slightly more direct run to Perimeter Park Drive. I would estimate departure by 7:30 a.m. Tuesday, allowing time for heavier traffic and finding the correct building. After you have seen the route once, 7:35 may be adequate. Holiday Inn Express is still workable, but its trip is a little more exposed to airport-area traffic.
Use the Hyatt House as the lodging choice. Do not reserve it yet. Note late arrival, direct booking, and the itemized folio requirement so those are checked when I have the authorization number.

Hyatt House Raleigh Durham Airport is selected for April 15-19, four nights, at the direct rate currently shown around $184 per night before tax. It is not reserved. Before booking, I will recheck that the rate remains below $210, confirm any parking and breakfast terms attached to that rate, add a late-arrival note, and verify that the front desk will issue an itemized folio separating room charges, taxes, and incidentals. The planned first-morning departure is 7:30 a.m. for the 8:00 a.m. audit start.
